headline: Iran strike reports lift WTI 2.9% to $102.78; Fed holds and the Treasury curve steepens
summary: A WSJ report that the US told Gulf allies to prepare for a short, intense campaign against Iran after the midterms, plus the Houthi claim on Ras Tanura, sent December WTI up $2.88 to $102.78 and Brent to $115.32, while RBOB lagged on a surprise 3.9 million barrel gasoline build. The Fed held at 3.75–4.00% with two hawkish dissents, but Warsh gave no December signal, so the 2-year slipped about 3bp to near 4.70% while the 10-year rose to about 5.02% as inflation compensation climbed. Gold recovered from a pre-Fed dip near $4,030 to about $4,065 as the dollar eased, silver stayed near $54, and Bunds and OATs edged higher in yield ahead of Thursday's ECB.
drivers: US readies options on Iran after the midterms

The WSJ said Washington told several Gulf states to prepare for a short, intense military campaign after Nov 3, and the Houthis claimed a missile hit on Saudi Arabia's 550,000 b/d Ras Tanura refinery. WTI settled up 2.9% at $102.78 after touching $103.55; Brent rose 1.3% to $115.32.
A Fed hold without a December promise

The FOMC held 10–2, with Cook and Hammack voting to hike, upgraded growth to 'strong' and said more information will guide its next step. Warsh avoided forward guidance, so the 2-year fell about 3bp to near 4.70% while the 10-year rose about 3bp to 5.02% and the 30-year about 5bp to 5.35%.
EIA: crude and diesel tighten, gasoline builds

Crude stocks fell 1.9 million barrels against a flat forecast and distillates fell 1.5 million to 10% below the five-year average, but gasoline rose 3.9 million against a 0.9 million draw as demand dropped 622,000 b/d. RBOB gained only 1.1% to $3.1734.

The 10-year Bund rose to about 3.37% in the morning with Treasuries and a 10-year Bund sale, while the OAT–Bund spread swung between about 156bp and 161bp. Markets price under 80% odds of a December ECB hike, down from near-certainty in September.

oil.note: Dec WTI settled up $2.88 (+2.9%) at $102.78 after a $103.55 high; Brent +1.3% at $115.32.
oil.why: Crude snapped a two-day slide as a WSJ report said the US told Gulf allies to prepare for a short, intense campaign against Iran after the Nov 3 midterms, and Iranian media claimed satellite images show Ras Tanura's main refining unit damaged, which Riyadh has not confirmed. EIA data added support: crude stocks fell 1.9 million barrels against a flat forecast, a fourth weekly draw, as exports jumped 1.4 million b/d. Iran's foreign minister saying diplomacy still has a chance trimmed the highs.
oil.outlook: Bias firm into the midterms: WTI $98–106, Brent $110–120. Confirmed damage at Ras Tanura or US strikes would test $106 and the April high of $112.95; passing Nov 3 without escalation would let the premium bleed back toward $98.
oil.watch: Iran diplomacy, Saudi damage reports, Dec Brent expiry Oct 30, OPEC+ Nov 1 and the US midterms Nov 3.

gas.note: Nov RBOB rose 3.58¢ (+1.1%) to $3.1734, lagging crude; down about 7.7% this month.
gas.why: Gasoline followed crude higher on the Iran escalation reports but rose less than half as much in percentage terms because the EIA showed a 3.9 million barrel stock build to 209.2 million, against forecasts for a 0.9 million draw, as implied demand fell 622,000 b/d to 8.36 million b/d. Refinery use slipped to 92.8%. Pump prices keep easing, with AAA's average near $4.25 against $4.48 a month ago, while Midwest stocks sit at record lows.
gas.outlook: Range $3.05–3.30. The gasoline crack is weakening, so RBOB should keep lagging crude; only a confirmed Gulf supply loss would take it above $3.30, and another build would pull it toward $3.05 once December becomes the front month.
gas.watch: Nov RBOB expiry Oct 30, the next EIA report Nov 4, AAA pump prices and Gulf headlines.

gold.note: Spot near $4,065, up about 0.2%, after a pre-Fed low near $4,030; Dec futures settled -0.6% at $4,051.60.
gold.why: Gold slipped about 0.7% to near $4,030 in early trade as higher oil revived inflation and rate-hike fears, then recovered after the Fed held and Warsh gave no December commitment, pulling the dollar down about 0.2% and the 2-year yield toward 4.70%. The rebound stayed modest because the vote had two dissents for a hike, December is still about 85% priced, and a Reuters poll showed analysts cutting 2026 gold forecasts on high yields.
gold.outlook: Range $3,990–4,110. A soft PCE on Thursday or post-midterm escalation that hits risk assets could carry it through $4,110; a hot PCE that cements December would retest $3,975, with $3,940, near the year's low, as the key floor.
gold.watch: Q3 GDP and PCE Oct 29, the ECB Oct 29, Iran headlines and the midterms Nov 3.

silver.note: Spot near $54.0, down about 0.8%, after dipping to $53.71; about $1.30 above the year's low.
silver.why: Silver underperformed gold again, sliding over 1% before the Fed as oil-driven rate-hike fears and doubts about industrial demand weighed, and it recovered less than gold after the decision. That kept the gold/silver ratio above 75, up from about 60 in January, as markets strip out silver's industrial and speculative premium faster than gold's monetary role. Platinum and palladium were also soft.
silver.outlook: Bias lower in a $52.50–56.00 range. A close below the $52.66 yearly low opens $50; a close above $56 would mark a base.
silver.watch: PCE Oct 29, big-tech earnings, China PMIs Oct 31 and the Fed's December pricing.

us2y.note: Down about 3bp to near 4.70% after spiking above 4.79% on the two hawkish dissents.
us2y.why: The 2-year jumped after the statement showed Cook and Hammack voting for a hike, then fell to about 4.69% as Warsh declined to signal December, said tighter credit shows 'monetary medicine' starting to work and added that inflation expectations remain anchored. Futures still price about an 85% chance of a December hike, but markets no longer fully price three hikes by end-2027, which pulled front-end yields lower.
us2y.outlook: Range 4.62–4.80%. A hot PCE or firm October payrolls would push it back toward 4.80%; a soft PCE or post-election risk-off would test 4.62%.
us2y.watch: Q3 GDP and PCE Oct 29, the 7-year auction Oct 29, ISM Nov 2 and payrolls Nov 6.

us5y.note: About 4.82%, little changed as the curve pivoted around the belly after the Fed.
us5y.why: The 5-year sat at the pivot of a steepening curve: lower odds of a long hiking cycle pulled short yields down while higher oil and inflation compensation lifted long ones. Tuesday's strong $70bn auction, cleared at 4.845% with a 2.33 bid-to-cover, still anchors demand in the sector, and the morning rise in oil after the Iran report was offset by Warsh's patient tone.
us5y.outlook: Range 4.74–4.92%. A hot PCE would push it toward 4.92%; a soft PCE or a risk-off move into the midterms would test 4.74%.
us5y.watch: PCE and the 7-year auction Oct 29 and payrolls Nov 6.

us10y.note: Up about 3bp to near 5.02% after touching 5.05% during Warsh's press conference.
us10y.why: The 10-year rose as the curve steepened: breakeven inflation climbed because traders read Warsh's choice to hold, despite hot September CPI and PPI, as tough talk without action, as MUFG's George Goncalves put it. Oil's 2.9% jump on the Iran reports added to inflation compensation. Yields eased back toward 5.00% late as Warsh stressed anchored expectations and the dollar slipped.
us10y.outlook: Range 4.92–5.12%. Holding above 5% is the base case while oil is above $100; a soft PCE plus no escalation after Nov 3 would test 4.92%, a hot PCE or US strikes on Iran 5.12%.
us10y.watch: PCE Oct 29, the midterms Nov 3, the Nov 4 refunding and payrolls Nov 6.

us30y.note: Up about 5bp to near 5.35%, leading the steepening.
us30y.why: The long bond sold off most as investors priced more inflation risk from a Fed seen tolerating elevated prices for now, with commentators such as Facet's Tom Graff arguing the Fed should have hiked. Higher oil added to the move. The UK's decision to cut long-dated gilt sales eased global term-premium worries slightly, focusing attention on whether Treasury trims long-end sizes at next week's refunding.
us30y.outlook: Range 5.25–5.45%. Smaller long-bond auctions on Nov 4 would help it rally; unchanged sizes plus oil above $105 would test 5.45%.
us30y.watch: The midterms Nov 3, the Nov 4 refunding and PCE Oct 29.

de2y.note: About 3.06%, slightly lower; under 80% odds of a December ECB hike priced before Thursday's meeting.
de2y.why: The Schatz edged lower as markets keep paring the case for near-term ECB hikes: Danske Bank noted December is now priced below 80%, against near-certainty for this meeting back in September, because higher Bund and OAT yields have tightened conditions on their own. Weak German consumer sentiment and the euro at a 17-month low near $1.111 kept buyers at the front end, offsetting the oil rally.
de2y.outlook: Range 2.98–3.15%. A Lagarde signal that December is live would lift it toward 3.15%; emphasis on tighter financing conditions would test 2.98%.
de2y.watch: The ECB decision Oct 29, flash October inflation Oct 30 and euro-area Q3 GDP.

de5y.note: About 3.19%, little changed as higher oil offset softer ECB pricing.
de5y.why: The 5-year Bund drifted sideways: the rebound in crude toward $115 Brent and the morning rise in Treasuries above 5% lifted yields, while fading ECB hike pricing and a haven bid during the French spread widening pulled them back. With inflation at 3.8% and the deposit rate at 2.50%, the belly is waiting for Lagarde's message.
de5y.outlook: Range 3.10–3.27%. A hawkish ECB pushes it to the top; renewed French stress or a dovish Lagarde caps it.
de5y.watch: The ECB Oct 29, euro inflation Oct 30 and the OAT–Bund spread.

de10y.note: About 3.36%, up about 1bp after reaching 3.37% in the morning; a 10-year Bund sale was absorbed.
de10y.why: The 10-year Bund followed Treasuries and gilts higher in the morning as oil jumped and investors positioned for the Fed, with a 10-year auction adding supply. The move faded as UK gilts rallied on a cautious budget that cut long-dated issuance, and some haven buying returned when French yields rose. Europe closed before Warsh spoke, so the US steepening is yet to be priced.
de10y.outlook: Range 3.28–3.45%. A hawkish ECB or oil above $120 Brent would lift it toward 3.45%; a dovish Lagarde or a French selloff would cap it.
de10y.watch: The ECB Oct 29, euro inflation Oct 30 and the US move after the Fed.

de30y.note: About 3.70%, flat as gilts rallied and oil rose.
de30y.why: The 30-year Bund was steady because two forces cancelled out: the oil rebound and firm Treasuries pushed long yields up, while the UK's move to cut 20- and 30-year gilt issuance, which took long gilt yields to a one-month low, eased term-premium worries across Europe. It tracks global long-end supply more than ECB pricing.
de30y.outlook: Range 3.62–3.80%. It follows the US 30-year and German supply; a selloff in long Treasuries after the refunding would test 3.80%.
de30y.watch: US long yields, the Nov 4 refunding and German long-dated auctions.

fr2y.note: About 3.70%, roughly steady after an intraday rise toward 3.77% as French selling resumed.
fr2y.why: Short French debt rose early as the Moody's relief rally kept fading and investors refocused on the 2027 budget fight, then settled back as the front end stays anchored by ECB pricing, where December hike odds are slipping. French consumer confidence at 80, matching its 2022 low, underlines the growth cost of higher yields and argues against further ECB tightening.
fr2y.outlook: Range 3.62–3.82%. It stays ECB-driven unless a budget defeat or censure threat reprices French credit risk into the front end.
fr2y.watch: The ECB Oct 29, French flash inflation and GDP Oct 30 and the budget debate.

fr5y.note: About 4.30%, little changed in a choppy pre-ECB session.
fr5y.why: The 5-year OAT was caught between renewed spread pressure in the morning and softer ECB pricing later. A 5.4% of GDP deficit, a fragmented parliament and street protests keep buyers selective, but some investors are adding at these levels after the Moody's hold at Aa3 with a negative outlook removed an immediate downgrade risk.
fr5y.outlook: Range 4.20–4.42%. A budget setback in parliament would send it toward 4.42%; reassurance from Lagarde would help it toward 4.20%.
fr5y.watch: The ECB Oct 29, French inflation and GDP Oct 30 and budget votes.

fr10y.note: About 4.92%, little changed after touching 4.965%; spread to Bunds near 156bp after 161bp intraday.
fr10y.why: The 10-year OAT rose in the morning as the Moody's relief faded and higher oil hit the euro, pushing the spread back to about 161bp and EUR/USD to a 17-month low. It retraced into the close as gilts rallied on the UK budget and investors waited for Lagarde, who is expected to be asked about French spreads, which have widened from about 90bp at the September ECB meeting.
fr10y.outlook: Spread range 148–170bp with a bias to hold 152–162bp. Language from Lagarde on preventing disorderly markets would narrow it toward 150bp; a failed budget vote or a fresh oil spike would put 170bp back in play.
fr10y.watch: The ECB Oct 29, French budget votes, French inflation Oct 30 and S&P's review Nov 27.

fr30y.note: About 5.40%, little changed and just below last week's highs.
fr30y.why: The 30-year OAT held steady as the UK's cut to long gilt issuance and a firmer risk tone offset higher oil. Investors still demand a large premium for long French debt through the budget fight and the 2027 presidential race, with debt near 120% of GDP leaving the long end the most exposed part of the curve.
fr30y.outlook: Range 5.30–5.55%. A credible budget deal would extend the rally; a close above 5.55% would signal renewed stress.
fr30y.watch: Budget votes, long-dated OAT auctions and the ECB Oct 29.

watch: Next: the ECB, US Q3 GDP, PCE and the 7-year auction Oct 29, euro inflation, Nov RBOB and Dec Brent expiry Oct 30, OPEC+ Nov 1, the US midterms Nov 3, the Nov 4 refunding and payrolls Nov 6.
